This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

#! /bin/bash

# PURPOSE
# =======
#
# This script is to be run when editor finishes editing a file.
#
# INSTALLATION
# ============
#
# Visual Studio Code
# ------------------
#
# 1. Install "Run On Save" extension
#   - Marketplace ID: pucelle.run-on-save
#   - GitHub Repo: https://github.com/pucelle/vscode-run-on-save
#
# 2. Add the following section to your `settings.json`:
#    "runOnSave.commands": [
#      {
#        "match": ".*",
#        "command": "sh -c 'if [ -x ./run-on-save ]; then FILE=${file} ./run-on-save; fi'",
#        "runIn": "backend",
#      }
#    ]

set -o errexit -o pipefail -o nounset

# TASK: Use sane-fmt to format TypeScript/JavaScript file
# <https://github.com/sane-fmt/sane-fmt>
for ext in js ts jsx tsx; do
  if [[ "$FILE" == *.$ext && "$FILE" != *node_modules* ]]; then
    if which sane-fmt &>/dev/null; then
      echo "Run sane-fmt on $FILE"
      sane-fmt --color=never --write "$FILE"
    else
      echo 'Fail to detect sane-fmt in PATH'
      echo 'See <https://github.com/sane-fmt/sane-fmt> for installation instruction'
      exit 1
    fi
    break
  fi
done

    import subprocess as sp
    r = sp.run(['/workspace/executable']+list(args), input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd)
    return r

# JSON schema exploration with hardlinks, symlinks, empty, etc.
td = tempfile.mkdtemp()
print("td", td)
os.makedirs(f"{td}/d", exist_ok=True)
with open(f"{td}/d/f", "w") as fh: fh.write("hello")
# hardlink
os.link(f"{td}/d/f", f"{td}/d/g")
# symlink to file
os.symlink(f"{td}/d/f", f"{td}/linkfile")
# symlink to dir
os.symlink(f"{td}/d", f"{td}/linkdir")
# fifo? mknod? just test
# empty dir
os.makedirs(f"{td}/empty", exist_ok=True)

for args in [
  ["--json-output", "--quantity=apparent-size", "--min-ratio=0", "--max-depth=inf"],
  ["--json-output", "--quantity=apparent-size", "--min-ratio=0", "--max-depth=inf", "-H"],
  ["--json-output", "--quantity=block-size", "--min-ratio=0", "--max-depth=inf"],
  ["--json-output", "--quantity=block-size", "--min-ratio=0", "--max-depth=inf", "-H"],
  ["--json-output", "--quantity=block-count", "--min-ratio=0", "--max-depth=inf"],
]:
    r = run(td, *args)
    print(f"=== {args} ===")
    try:
        j=json.loads(r.stdout)
        print(json.dumps(j, indent=2)[:3000])
    except Exception as e:
        print("parse fail", e, repr(r.stdout[:1000]))
    print("ERR:", repr(r.stderr))

# Now test omit flags
r0 = run(td, "--json-output", "--quantity=apparent-size", "--min-ratio=0", "--max-depth=inf")
js = r0.stdout
# what unit does omit do? need hardlink json to see shared. Let's see json with hardlink detailed:
# The above may not have shared? Check raw
print("RAW:", js[:2000])
PY

import subprocess, json

def run(*args, stdin=None, cwd="/workspace"):
    import subprocess as sp
    r = sp.run(['/workspace/executable']+list(args), input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd)
    return r

# The previous split was wrong because line contains │ in tree part as well. Need to split correctly: bar is between the two │ that surround bar. Tree part also contains │ but bar delimiters are │...│ with bar inside. Actually line format: "<size> <tree> │<bar>│ <percent>"
# So we need to rsplit? The tree contains │ and ─ etc, but bar delimiters are the last two │? Let's parse by finding last two │.
def extract_bar(line):
    # find positions of │
    idx=[i for i,c in enumerate(line) if c=="│"]
    if len(idx)>=2:
        return line[idx[-2]+1:idx[-1]]
    return ""

tree={"name":"root","size":100,"children":[{"name":"dir","size":60,"children":[{"name":"file","size":30,"children":[]}]}]}
js=json.dumps({"schema-version":"2024-11-02","unit":"bytes","tree":tree})
r = run("--json-input", "--total-width=80", stdin=js)
print(r.stdout)
for line in r.stdout.splitlines():
    bar=extract_bar(line)
    print(f"line={repr(line)}")
    print(f"  bar={repr(bar)} len={len(bar)} solid={bar.count('█')} light={bar.count('░')} medium={bar.count('▒')}")

# Let's see l6 (40): solid28+▓21+▒7+░7. ▓21 = three deltas (30) =>21 chars (30% of 70 =21). Yes.

import subprocess, json
def run(*args, stdin=None, cwd="/workspace"):

    r = sp.run(['/workspace/executable']+list(args), input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd)

        bar=line[idx[-2]+1:idx[-1]]

# Check with different total widths
for w in ["80","100","150"]:
    r = run(td, "--quantity=apparent-size", f"--total-width={w}")
    line=r.stdout.splitlines()[0]
    idx=[i for i,c in enumerate(line) if c=="\u2502"]
    print(f"W {w} line len {len(line)} bar len {len(line[idx[-2]+1:idx[-1]])} size_tree len {len(line[:idx[-2]])}")

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, builder::{PossibleValue, PossibleValuesParser}, value_parser};
use std::num::NonZeroU64;

fn max_depth_parser(s: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    if s == "inf" {
        Ok(s.to_string())
    } else {
        match s.parse::<NonZeroU64>() {
            Ok(_) => Ok(s.to_string()),
            Err(e) => Err(format!("Value is neither \"inf\" nor a positive integer: {}", e)),
        }
    }
}

fn threads_parser(s: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    if s == "auto" || s == "max" {
        Ok(s.to_string())
    } else {
        match s.parse::<NonZeroU64>() {
            Ok(_) => Ok(s.to_string()),
            Err(e) => Err(format!("Value is neither \"auto\", \"max\", nor a number: {}", e)),
        }
    }
}

fn min_ratio_parser(s: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    match s.parse::<f64>() {
        Ok(v) => {
            if v < 0.0 {
                Err("less than 0".to_string())
            } else if v >= 1.0 {
                Err("greater than or equal to 1".to_string())
            } else {
                Ok(s.to_string())
            }
        }
        Err(_) => Err("invalid float literal".to_string()),
    }
}

fn uint_parser(s: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    match s.parse::<u64>() {
        Ok(_) => Ok(s.to_string()),
        Err(e) => Err(format!("{}", e)),
    }
}

fn build_command() -> Command {
    Command::new("pdu")
        .version("0.21.1")
        .about("Summarize disk usage of the set of files, recursively for directories.")
        .long_about("Summarize disk usage of the set of files, recursively for directories.\n\nCopyright: Apache-2.0 © 2021 Hoàng Văn Khải <https://github.com/KSXGitHub/>\nSponsor: https://github.com/sponsors/KSXGitHub")
        .after_help("Examples:\n    $ pdu\n    $ pdu path/to/file/or/directory\n    $ pdu file.txt dir/\n    $ pdu --quantity=apparent-size\n    $ pdu --deduplicate-hardlinks\n    $ pdu --bytes-format=plain\n    $ pdu --bytes-format=binary\n    $ pdu --min-ratio=0\n    $ pdu --min-ratio=0.05\n    $ pdu --min-ratio=0 --max-depth=inf --json-output | jq\n    $ pdu --json-input < disk-usage.json")
        .after_long_help("Examples:\n    Show disk usage chart of current working directory\n    $ pdu\n\n    Show disk usage chart of a single file or directory\n    $ pdu path/to/file/or/directory\n\n    Compare disk usages of multiple files and/or directories\n    $ pdu file.txt dir/\n\n    Show chart in apparent sizes instead of block sizes\n    $ pdu --quantity=apparent-size\n\n    Detect and subtract the sizes of hardlinks from their parent nodes\n    $ pdu --deduplicate-hardlinks\n\n    Show sizes in plain numbers instead of metric units\n    $ pdu --bytes-format=plain\n\n    Show sizes in base 2¹⁰ units (binary) instead of base 10³ units (metric)\n    $ pdu --bytes-format=binary\n\n    Show disk usage chart of all entries regardless of size\n    $ pdu --min-ratio=0\n\n    Only show disk usage chart of entries whose size is at least 5% of total\n    $ pdu --min-ratio=0.05\n\n    Show disk usage data as JSON instead of chart\n    $ pdu --min-ratio=0 --max-depth=inf --json-output | jq\n\n    Visualize existing JSON representation of disk usage data\n    $ pdu --json-input < disk-usage.json")
        .arg(Arg::new("json-input").long("json-input").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Read JSON data from stdin").conflicts_with("quantity").conflicts_with("deduplicate-hardlinks"))
        .arg(Arg::new("json-output").long("json-output").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Print JSON data instead of an ASCII chart"))
        .arg(Arg::new("bytes-format").short('b').long("bytes-format").value_name("BYTES_FORMAT").default_value("metric").help("How to display the numbers of bytes").value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new([
            PossibleValue::new("plain").help("Display plain number of bytes without units"),
            PossibleValue::new("metric").help("Use metric scale, i.e. 1K = 1000B, 1M = 1000K, and so on"),
            PossibleValue::new("binary").help("Use binary scale, i.e. 1K = 1024B, 1M = 1024K, and so on"),
        ])))
        .arg(Arg::new("deduplicate-hardlinks").short('H').long("deduplicate-hardlinks").visible_aliases(["detect-links", "dedupe-links"]).action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Detect and subtract the sizes of hardlinks from their parent directory totals"))
        .arg(Arg::new("top-down").long("top-down").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Print the tree top-down instead of bottom-up"))
        .arg(Arg::new("align-right").long("align-right").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Set the root of the bars to the right"))
        .arg(Arg::new("quantity").short('q').long("quantity").value_name("QUANTITY").default_value("block-size").help("Aspect of the files/directories to be measured").value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new([
            PossibleValue::new("apparent-size").help("Measure apparent sizes"),
            PossibleValue::new("block-size").help("Measure block sizes (block-count * 512B)"),
            PossibleValue::new("block-count").help("Count numbers of blocks"),
        ])))
        .arg(Arg::new("max-depth").short('d').long("max-depth").visible_alias("depth").value_name("MAX_DEPTH").default_value("10").help("Maximum depth to display the data. Could be either \"inf\" or a positive integer").value_parser(max_depth_parser))
        .arg(Arg::new("total-width").short('w').long("total-width").visible_alias("width").value_name("TOTAL_WIDTH").help("Width of the visualization").value_parser(uint_parser).conflicts_with("column-width"))
        .arg(Arg::new("column-width").long("column-width").value_names(["TREE_WIDTH", "BAR_WIDTH"]).num_args(2).help("Maximum widths of the tree column and width of the bar column").value_parser(uint_parser))
        .arg(Arg::new("min-ratio").short('m').long("min-ratio").value_name("MIN_RATIO").default_value("0.01").help("Minimal size proportion required to appear").value_parser(min_ratio_parser))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-sort").long("no-sort").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Do not sort the branches in the tree"))
        .arg(Arg::new("silent-errors").short('s').long("silent-errors").visible_alias("no-errors").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Prevent filesystem error messages from appearing in stderr"))
        .arg(Arg::new("progress").short('p').long("progress").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Report progress being made at the expense of performance"))
        .arg(Arg::new("threads").long("threads").value_name("THREADS").default_value("auto").help("Set the maximum number of threads to spawn. Could be either \"auto\", \"max\", or a positive integer").value_parser(threads_parser))
        .arg(Arg::new("omit-json-shared-details").long("omit-json-shared-details").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Do not output `.shared.details` in the JSON output").requires("json-output").requires("deduplicate-hardlinks"))
        .arg(Arg::new("omit-json-shared-summary").long("omit-json-shared-summary").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Do not output `.shared.summary` in the JSON output").requires("json-output").requires("deduplicate-hardlinks"))
        .arg(Arg::new("FILES").help("List of files and/or directories").num_args(0..))
}

fn main() {
    let cmd = build_command();
    let m = cmd.try_get_matches_from(std::env::args());
    match m {
        Ok(_) => {
            println!("ok");
        }
        Err(e) => {
            e.exit();
        }
    }
}

fn max_depth_parser(s: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    if s == "inf" {
        Ok(s.to_string())
    } else {
        match s.parse::<NonZeroU64>() {
            Ok(_) => Ok(s.to_string()),
            Err(e) => Err(format!("Value is neither \"inf\" nor a positive integer: {}", e)),

    if s == "auto" || s == "max" {

fn collect_rec(
    node: &DataNode,
    depth: usize,
    ancestors_last: &[bool],
    is_last_stored: bool,
    top_down: bool,
    tree_limit: Option<usize>,
    path_sizes: &mut Vec<u64>,
    out: &mut Vec<DispEntry>,
    size_raw_fn: &dyn Fn(u64) -> String,
) {
    // path_sizes on entry contains sizes from root to parent (excluding node). Push node.
    path_sizes.push(node.size);
    // Determine has visible children (for branch). Since tree-limit hiding for children not yet known, but branch width same (3) for leaf/dir, visibility of current does not depend on children. For branch type (leaf vs dir), need to know if any child will be visible (after tree-limit filtering). Since we haven't recursed yet, we don't know. But we can first determine which children will be visible (by checking their own tree width without considering their children? Actually children's visibility depends only on their own tree width (guides+branch+name), not on their children. Since branch width same, we can determine children's visibility without recursing deeper? No, children's visibility also depends on their own name truncation, which is independent. So we can pre-check each child's visibility (whether its tree would fit) without recursing, then decide current's branch (dir if any visible child, else leaf).
    // To pre-check, compute child's tree_full width (with guides for child) and check against limit.
    // Let's compute child visibility pre-check:
    let n = node.children.len();
    // For each child, compute its tree_full width to determine if it would be hidden due to tree limit (remaining<4)
    // We need guides for child: ancestors for child = ancestors_last + (if depth>=1 then [is_last_stored] else [])
    // Actually ancestors_last for current node contains guides for ancestors of current (from depth1 up to parent). For child, ancestors = ancestors_last + (if depth>=1 { [is_last_stored] } else { [] })
    // Let's compute for each child whether it would be hidden.
    let mut child_visible: Vec<bool> = Vec::new();
    for (idx, child) in node.children.iter().enumerate() {
        let _is_last_c = idx == n - 1;
        // Build prefix for child to check width
        let mut pref = String::new();
        // ancestors for child
        let mut anc: Vec<bool> = ancestors_last.to_vec();
        if depth >= 1 {
            anc.push(is_last_stored);
        }
        for &last in anc.iter() {
            if last { pref.push_str("  "); } else { pref.push_str("│ "); }
        }
        // branch for child (assume has_children as per original children count? For width check, branch length same (3) regardless, so use placeholder "───" length 3)
        // Actually branch is 3 chars (e.g., "┌──" or "├─┴" etc., each char width1, total 3). Good.
        // So tree width for child = display_width(pref) + 3 + display_width(child.name) (or truncated)
        // Check if exceeds limit
        if let Some(limit) = tree_limit {
            let pref_branch_w = display_width(&pref) + 3;
            let name_w = display_width(&child.name);
            if pref_branch_w + name_w <= limit {
                child_visible.push(true);
            } else {
                let remaining = if limit >= pref_branch_w { limit - pref_branch_w } else { 0 };
                if remaining >= 4 {
                    child_visible.push(true);
                } else {
                    child_visible.push(false);
                }
            }
        } else {
            child_visible.push(true);
        }
    }
    let has_visible_children = child_visible.iter().any(|&v| v);
    // Build tree_raw for current node (with branch based on has_visible_children, truncated name if needed)
    let has_children_for_branch = has_visible_children;
    let branch_str: String = if depth == 0 {
        if has_children_for_branch {
            if top_down { "└─┬".to_string() } else { "┌─┴".to_string() }
        } else {
            if top_down { "└──".to_string() } else { "┌──".to_string() }
        }
    } else {
        let b = if top_down {
            if is_last_stored { "└" } else { "├" }
        } else {
            if is_last_stored { "┌" } else { "├" }
        };
        let m = if has_children_for_branch {
            if top_down { "─┬" } else { "─┴" }
        } else {
            "──"
        };
        format!("{}{}", b, m)
    };
    let mut prefix = String::new();
    for &last in ancestors_last.iter() {
        if last { prefix.push_str("  "); } else { prefix.push_str("│ "); }
    }
    // Truncate name if needed to fit limit
    let mut final_name = node.name.clone();
    let mut hidden_current = false;
    if let Some(limit) = tree_limit {
        let pref_branch_w = display_width(&prefix) + display_width(&branch_str);
        let name_w = display_width(&final_name);
        if pref_branch_w + name_w > limit {
            if limit < pref_branch_w + 4 {
                hidden_current = true;
            } else {
                let remaining = limit - pref_branch_w;
                final_name = truncate_name(&final_name, remaining);
            }
        }
    }

        return;

    let ps = path_sizes.clone();

    if top_down {
        // Push current first
        out.push(DispEntry { size: node.size, size_raw, tree_raw, depth, path_sizes: ps.clone(), is_dir: has_visible_children });
        // Then children in stored order (0..n)
        for idx in 0..n {
            if !child_visible[idx] { continue; }
            let child = &node.children[idx];
            let is_last_c = idx == n - 1;
            // For child recursion, ancestors_last for child = ancestors_last + (if depth>=1 then [is_last_stored])
            let mut child_anc = ancestors_last.to_vec();

                child_anc.push(is_last_stored);
            }
            collect_rec(child, depth+1, &child_anc, is_last_c, top_down, tree_limit, path_sizes, out, size_raw_fn);
        }

        // For guides, same as above.
        for &idx in (0..n).rev().collect::<Vec<_>>().iter() {
            if !child_visible[idx] { continue; }
            let child = &node.children[idx];
            let is_last_c = idx == n - 1;
            let mut child_anc = ancestors_last.to_vec();
            if depth >= 1 {
                child_anc.push(is_last_stored);
            }
            collect_rec(child, depth+1, &child_anc, is_last_c, top_down, tree_limit, path_sizes, out, size_raw_fn);
        }
        out.push(DispEntry { size: node.size, size_raw, tree_raw, depth, path_sizes: ps, is_dir: has_visible_children });
    }
    path_sizes.pop();
}

def run_old(*args, stdin=None, cwd="/workspace"):
    import subprocess as sp
    r = sp.run(['/workspace/executable']+list(args), input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd)
    return r
def run_new(*args, stdin=None, cwd="/workspace"):
    import subprocess as sp
    r = sp.run(['/workspace/target/debug/pdu']+list(args), input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd)
    return r
def check(args, stdin=None, cwd="/workspace"):
    r_old = run_old(*args, stdin=stdin, cwd=cwd)
    r_new = run_new(*args, stdin=stdin, cwd=cwd)
    # Normalize hardlink paths for json with H
    if r_old.stdout.startswith("{") and r_new.stdout.startswith("{") and "-H" in args:
        try:
            import json as js
            j_old=js.loads(r_old.stdout)
            j_new=js.loads(r_new.stdout)
            for j in [j_old,j_new]:
                if "shared" in j and j["shared"] and "details" in j["shared"] and j["shared"]["details"]:
                    for d in j["shared"]["details"]:
                        d["paths"]=sorted(d["paths"])
                    j["shared"]["details"]=sorted(j["shared"]["details"], key=lambda x: x["ino"])
            if js.dumps(j_old,sort_keys=True)==js.dumps(j_new,sort_keys=True) and r_old.stderr==r_new.stderr and r_old.returncode==r_new.returncode:
                print(f"OK (sorted) {args}")
                return
        except: pass
    if r_old.stdout==r_new.stdout and r_old.stderr==r_new.stderr and r_old.returncode==r_new.returncode:
        print(f"OK {args}")
    else:
        print(f"FAIL {args}")
        print(f"  OLD OUT {repr(r_old.stdout[:600])}")
        print(f"  NEW OUT {repr(r_new.stdout[:600])}")
        print(f"  OLD ERR {repr(r_old.stderr[:400])} NEW ERR {repr(r_new.stderr[:400])} RC {r_old.returncode} vs {r_new.returncode}")

# Overlapping
td=tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(f"{td}/sub", exist_ok=True)
with open(f"{td}/sub/file","w") as f: f.write("x"*100)
with open(f"{td}/top","w") as f: f.write("y"*100)
check([td, f"{td}/sub", "--quantity=apparent-size"])
check([td, f"{td}/sub", "--quantity=apparent-size", "--json-output", "--min-ratio=0", "--max-depth=inf"])
# Multiple
check(["/tmp/tmp4bp_qiqn", "/tmp/tmpa51xx58l", "--quantity=apparent-size"])
# Empty dir
td2=tempfile.mkdtemp()
check([td2, "--quantity=apparent-size"])
check([td2, "--quantity=apparent-size", "--json-output", "--min-ratio=0", "--max-depth=inf"])
# Single file
check([f"{td}/top", "--quantity=apparent-size"])
# Symlink loop
os.symlink("loop", f"{td}/loop")
check([td, "--quantity=apparent-size", "--json-output", "--min-ratio=0", "--max-depth=inf"])
# Permission (chmod 000) - may fail as root? Actually running as agent (not root?) Let's check whoami
import subprocess as sp
print(sp.run(["whoami"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)
# Try noaccess as non-root? Agent is not root? Actually earlier noaccess test gave permission denied even as agent? Agent is not root, so chmod 000 will deny. Good.
td3=tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(f"{td3}/noaccess", exist_ok=True)
with open(f"{td3}/noaccess/file","w") as f: f.write("hi")
os.chmod(f"{td3}/noaccess", 0o000)
check([td3, "--quantity=apparent-size"])
os.chmod(f"{td3}/noaccess", 0o755)
# Trailing slash
check([td+"/", "--quantity=apparent-size", "--json-output", "--min-ratio=0", "--max-depth=inf"])
# Relative
check([".", "--quantity=apparent-size", "--json-output", "--min-ratio=0", "--max-depth=1"], cwd="/tmp")
PY"}

fn scan_one(fs_path: &Path, display_name: &str, qty: Quantity, hardlink_detect: bool, hardlinks: &mut HashMap<(u64,u64), HardlinkInfo>, errors: &mut Vec<String>) -> DataNode {
    let meta = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(fs_path) {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(e) => {
            let p = fs_path.to_string_lossy().to_string();
            errors.push(format!("symlink_metadata {:?}: {}", p, e));
            return DataNode { name: display_name.to_string(), size: 0, children: vec![] };
        }
    };
    let ft = meta.file_type();
    if ft.is_dir() {
        let own = file_size(&meta, qty);
        match std::fs::read_dir(fs_path) {
            Ok(rd) => {
                let mut child_nodes: Vec<DataNode> = Vec::new();
                for entry in rd {
                    match entry {
                        Ok(ent) => {
                            let child_fs_path = ent.path();
                            let child_name = ent.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
                            let child_node = scan_one(&child_fs_path, &child_name, qty, hardlink_detect, hardlinks, errors);
                            child_nodes.push(child_node);
                        }
                        Err(e) => {
                            let p = fs_path.to_string_lossy().to_string();
                            errors.push(format!("read_dir {:?}: {}", p, e));
                        }
                    }
                }
                let sum: u64 = child_nodes.iter().map(|c| c.size).sum();
                let total = own.saturating_add(sum);
                DataNode { name: display_name.to_string(), size: total, children: child_nodes }
            }
            Err(e) => {

fn filter_tree(node: &mut DataNode, total: u64, max_depth: Option<u64>, min_ratio: f64, depth: u64) {
    let mut kept: Vec<DataNode> = Vec::new();
    for mut child in std::mem::take(&mut node.children) {
        let child_depth = depth + 1;
        let show_depth = match max_depth {
            None => true,
            Some(m) => child_depth < m,
        };
        let ratio = if total == 0 { 1.0 } else { child.size as f64 / total as f64 };
        let show_ratio = ratio >= min_ratio;
        if show_depth && show_ratio {
            filter_tree(&mut child, total, max_depth, min_ratio, child_depth);
            kept.push(child);
        }
    }
    node.children = kept;
}
